facts.text: Copy-v0 is registered with entry point gym.envs.algorithmic:CopyEnv and max_episode_steps=200
The action space is a three-tuple of Discrete spaces: left or right movement, a write flag with 2 values, and a character in 0 .. base - 1
The observation space is Discrete(base + 1): the character under the read head, and the blank index base when the head is out of bounds
The movements are left and right and the read head starts at index 0
The observation is the input character at the read head; a position below 0 or past the tape returns the blank index base
A correct write earns +1, a wrong character earns -0.5 and ends the episode, and a step without a write earns 0
The episode also ends when the write head reaches the target length, and a step that passes the time limit earns -1 and ends the episode
The time limit is input_width + len(target) + 4 steps
A reset draws a tape length of randint(3) + min_length and derives the target from that tape
The Copy task's target is the input tape itself
The minimum tape length starts at 2 (AlgorithmicEnv's starting_min_length default)
The environment raises min_length by one after its promotion window and caps it at 30
AlgorithmicEnv.seed seeds the environment from gym.utils.seeding
CopyEnv's constructor defaults are base=5 and chars=True

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the fake's tape; the dynamics of the tape and write head are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions.  This package's fake draws tapes with Python's random.Random and upstream with numpy's RandomState (algorithmic_env.py:91-93), so one seed gives different tapes on the two

gaps: the model is an algorithmic input tape and write head, not a physical device: no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, actuators, sensors or noise are modelled
event-driven analytic model: timestep_ms 0 means no wall-clock or simulated duration advances; one step is one discrete transition, and only commands advance the world
the fake draws tapes with Python's random.Random while upstream draws them with numpy's RandomState from gym.utils.seeding, so a seed does not give the same tape on the two implementations

the registered TimeLimit wrapper with max_episode_steps=200 is not modelled; the environment's own time limit (input_width + len(target) + 4, at most 68 with the 30-character cap) ends an episode first
the fake is a re-implementation of CopyEnv and AlgorithmicEnv and was not compared with the upstream environment, which was never imported or installed where the gate ran
no rendering, PassiveEnvChecker or OrderEnforcing wrapper is modelled; the bridge serves the raw environment API
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state
the bridge derives the action schema from a Tuple space without per-element limits, so the three action elements are checked by the environment's own assertion, not by the runtime envelope
autoreset is enabled: after terminated or truncated, the next step starts a new episode, while the output still reports the terminal flags of the last tick

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
